spread-list-1
# A LIST'S NON-ELEMENTS DO NOT CONSUME A PATH INDEX (BUGS.md 44).
# A `&:` spread constrains the elements and a `k:v` pair in list
# position is not one, so neither is an element and neither may take an
# index. Generation always agreed -- the array is built right in both
# ports -- but @tabnas/path's `@elem-ao` increments its index for every
# elem rule, so in TypeScript each non-element stole one and every LATER
# element's path came out one too high. `[&:integer,10,20,"bad"]` named
# `$.a.3` while `aontu get $.a.2` returned the offending value, and on a
# one-element list the path pointed past the end. Go was right
# throughout.
# These rows assert the PATH, not just the code. That is the point of
# them: both ports emitted `no_scalar_unify` all along, so a code-only
# row -- which is what nearly every error row in this suite is -- agreed
# in both engines while the paths disagreed. The path is the field
# `vet --format json` hands an agent.
# Every expectation below was obtained by running BOTH engines and
# diffing, per the parity probe. Cases where the two ports still
# disagree are deliberately NOT here: a `k:v` pair written BEFORE a `&:`
# spread makes TypeScript drop the spread entirely, and a conjunct of
# unequal-length lists paths its finding differently. Both predate this
# fix (verified against the published 0.53.0) and neither is this rule.
